title: James Rothman reconstructed the cell's transport system in a test tube, discovered SNARE and won the Nobel Prize

trailer.text: James Rothman is an American biochemist and cell biologist at the Yale School of Medicine, and a laureate of the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
As a young group leader at Stanford, he reconstructed in a test tube the way vesicles move inside the cell.
He purified the proteins NSF and SNAP, and with their help found in brain tissue proteins that he named SNAREs.
According to the Nobel announcement, proteins on the vesicle and on the target membrane bind to each other like the two sides of a zipper.
In 2013 Rothman received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, together with Randy Schekman and Thomas Südhof.

glance.label: The first moment
glance.value: 1979, reconstruction of transport in a test tube

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: Nobel Prize in Medicine 2013, with Schekman and Südhof

paragraphs.text: Rothman said that from an early age he wanted to be a scientist, especially a physicist.
His father, Martin Rothman, was a pediatrician, and Rothman described him as an intellectually oriented small-town physician.
In 1971 Rothman completed a bachelor's degree in physics at Yale, summa cum laude.
In 1976 he received a doctorate from Harvard Medical School, and afterwards he was a postdoctoral fellow at MIT.
According to him, it was in his first year of medical school that he first learned about the secretory pathway.
He asked how cells make vesicles, how each vesicle knows where to go and how it fuses.
According to the Nobel announcement, each cell is a factory that produces and exports molecules.
The Nobel Committee wrote that the precise way in which the vesicles find their destination and fuse with organelles or with the cell membrane remained a mystery.
According to Science News, before the three laureates no one knew how cells move packets of material to their destination.
According to the Nobel announcement, without this precise organization the cell would lapse into chaos.

stations.title: At Stanford: transport in a test tube

paragraphs.text: Rothman joined the Department of Biochemistry at Stanford as a junior faculty member.
According to the King Faisal Prize website, within six years he rose there to the rank of full professor.
He said that there he asked Arthur Kornberg why he chose to study the problem of DNA synthesis.
According to a review in PMC, both Rothman and Schekman were inspired by Kornberg.
As a young group leader at Stanford, Rothman developed an in vitro reconstitution assay for intracellular vesicle transport.
According to Science News, he broke open hamster ovary cells and reconstructed the transport in a test tube.
According to the King Faisal Prize website, he showed that transport within the Golgi could be reconstructed from isolated Golgi membranes, cytosol and ATP.
According to him, after he and Erik Fries first published transport in a cell-free system, they had great difficulty repeating their exact results, and it would have been easy to be discouraged.
When they solved the difficulty, he said, they discovered that they had reconstituted vesicle transport within the Golgi, a process not previously known.
According to him, in 1984 three pivotal papers by his group appeared in Cell describing cell-free transport between Golgi stacks.

stations.title: NSF, SNAP and the cell's zipper

paragraphs.text: According to Science News, Rothman discovered that the chemical N-ethylmaleimide disrupts the transport process.
The first protein he purified was NSF, and the next in line was SNAP.
According to Britannica, Rothman and his colleagues identified NSF and the SNAP family of proteins in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
Rothman then used NSF and SNAP as bait, turned to brain tissue and purified from it proteins that he named SNAREs.
According to the Yale profile, he discovered the complex of SNARE proteins in 1993.
According to the Kavli Prize website, in the same year he performed the key experiment that linked his work to that of Südhof and Scheller.
Rothman proposed the SNARE hypothesis.
According to the Nobel announcement, proteins on the vesicle and on the target membrane bind to each other like the two sides of a zipper.
Rothman showed that the system is highly specific: a particular t-SNARE interacts only with one, or with a few, of the possible v-SNAREs.
Rothman wrote that without Felix Wieland it is doubtful whether NSF, SNAP, SNAREs or coatomer would have been discovered.

stations.title: Schekman in yeast, Südhof in nerve cells

paragraphs.text: In the 1970s Randy Schekman decided to study the genetic basis of the cell's transport system, using yeast as a model system.
According to Science News, in 1976 he began searching for the transport molecules in yeast.
According to an article in JCB, at that time few thought that yeast was capable of secretion, or that its activities had anything to do with mechanisms in animal cells.
Schekman reasoned that some of the mutations might be lethal, and therefore used temperature-sensitive mutants.
In yeast cells with a defective transport mechanism, vesicles piled up in certain parts of the cell.
In the first screen Schekman identified two genes, sec1 and sec2, and after the screen was refined a further 23 genes were identified, which were assigned to three classes.
According to a review in PMC, Schekman's approach made it possible to identify more than 50 proteins involved in transport at different stages of the secretory pathway.
The two paths met: the yeast mutant sec18 corresponded to the NSF that Rothman had purified, and this pointed to an ancient evolutionary origin of the mechanism.
According to a review in PMC, the convergence of the genetic approach and the biochemical approach demonstrated the robustness of both.
Vesicle transport and fusion operate with the same general principles in different organisms, such as yeast and man.
Thomas Südhof identified molecular machinery that responds to an influx of calcium ions and directs neighbouring proteins to bind vesicles to the outer membrane of the nerve cell.
He discovered that the proteins complexin and synaptotagmin are critical to calcium-mediated vesicle fusion.
According to Science News, the three researchers worked independently.
According to the Nobel announcement, disturbances in this system contribute to neurological diseases, diabetes and immunological disorders.
According to the Yale profile, damage to the fusion process can cause metabolic, neuropsychiatric and other diseases.
Südhof showed that deletion of Munc18-1 in mice leads to a complete loss of neurotransmitter secretion from synaptic vesicles.
According to the Committee, in certain forms of epilepsy mutations have been described in the gene encoding MUNC-18-1.
According to the Committee, in type 2 diabetes there are defects in insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells.
In FHL patients, according to the Committee, natural killer cells are not properly regulated, and this leads to hyperinflammation, which can be lethal.
Defects in the transport process lead to a variety of conditions, including diabetes and botulism.
According to the Committee, botulism is a paralytic disease caused by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum.
On 7 October 2013, people in the field woke up to the news that Rothman, Schekman and Südhof had won the Nobel Prize.
The Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to the three of them "for their discoveries of machinery regulating vesicle traffic, a major transport system in our cells".
The prize is awarded by the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet, which consists of 50 professors.
According to Science News, Schekman is affiliated with Berkeley, Rothman with the Yale School of Medicine and Südhof with Stanford.
According to a scientist quoted in Science News, the laureates identified the "dispatcher" molecules that direct the traffic.
According to an article in JCB, the scientific dynamic that Rothman and Schekman generated gave the field focus and excitement.
According to Britannica, Rothman won the Gairdner International Award in 1996 and the Lasker Award in 2002, both together with Schekman.
According to the Kavli Prize website, in 2010 he received the Kavli Prize in Neuroscience.
In 2019 he was elected a Foreign Member of the Royal Society of London.

stations.title: The path, the home and the people

paragraphs.text: In 1988 Rothman moved to Princeton, to the Department of Molecular Biology.

In 2008 he joined the faculty of Yale in New Haven, Connecticut; according to the 2013 Nobel Prize announcement, he was Professor and Chairman in the Department of Cell Biology there, and according to the Kavli Prize website, he was Professor and Chairman in the Department of Chemistry.
Rothman is married and has a daughter and a son.
He wrote that his wife, Joy Hirsch, was his critic and also his supporter in the early years, when his work was not accepted as it is today.
On 10 December 2013, immediately after the Nobel Prize Ceremony, he was photographed with his children in the Concert Hall in Stockholm.
That same year he met President Obama, at a meeting of American Nobel laureates and their spouses.
According to the Yale School of Medicine website, Rothman served as Chair of the Department of Cell Biology (2008–2023).
Rothman himself wrote that a hypothesis he developed with Graham Warren at Stanford turned out to be bold but ultimately wrong.
According to an article in JCB, some of Rothman's interpretations were disputed, but there was no dispute about the importance of the components that were identified.
According to the same article, the principle that the transport mechanism is universal was not weakened despite the disputes over the years.
According to an article in JCB, others, for example Scheller and Novick, could also have been included in the prize, but it may be given to only three, and the three laureates are fully deserving.
According to a review in PMC, some argue that research on intracellular traffic is a field that has reached maturity, but the author believes it is far from waning.

claims.text: סודהוף הראה שמחיקת Munc18-1 בעכברים גורמת לאובדן מלא של הפרשת מוליכים עצביים משלפוחיות סינפטיות.
claims.quote: Südhof showed that deletion of Munc18-1 in mice leads to a complete loss of neurotransmitter secretion from synaptic vesicles

claims.text: לפי הוועדה, בצורות מסוימות של אפילפסיה תוארו מוטציות בגן המקודד ל-MUNC-18-1.
claims.quote: in certain forms of epilepsy, mutations in the gene encoding MUNC-18-1 have been described

claims.text: לפי הוועדה, בסוכרת מסוג 2 יש פגמים בהפרשת אינסולין מתאי בטא של הלבלב.
claims.quote: type 2 diabetes are characterized by defects in both insulin secretion from pancreatic beta-cells

claims.text: לפי הוועדה, בחולי FHL תאי הורג טבעיים אינם מוסדרים כראוי, מה שמוביל לדלקת יתר שעלולה להיות קטלנית.
claims.quote: In FHL patients, natural killer cells fail to regulate properly when encountering target cells, leading to hyperinflammation, which can be lethal.

claims.text: לפי הוועדה, בוטוליזם נגרם מהחיידק Clostridium botulinum והוא מחלה משתקת.
claims.quote: Botulism, caused by the anaerobic bacterium Clostridium botulinum, is a paralytic disease

claims.text: ב-7 באוקטובר 2013 התעוררו אנשי התחום לבשורה שרותמן, שקמן וסודהוף זכו בפרס.
claims.quote: The morning of October 7th, 2013, we woke up to the exciting news that James Rothman, Randy Schekman and Thomas Südhof had been awarded

claims.text: פרס נובל ברפואה מוענק על ידי אסיפת נובל של מכון קרולינסקה, המורכבת מ-50 פרופסורים.
claims.quote: The Nobel Assembly, consisting of 50 professors at Karolinska Institutet, awards the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

claims.text: לפי Science News, שקמן משויך לברקלי, רותמן לבית הספר לרפואה של ייל וסודהוף לסטנפורד.
claims.quote: The Nobel committee selected Randy Schekman of the University of California, Berkeley, James Rothman of the Yale School of Medicine, and Thomas Südhof of Stanford University to share the award.

claims.text: לפי מדען שצוטט ב-Science News, הזוכים זיהו את מולקולות ה״מוקדן״ שמכוונות את התנועה.
claims.quote: the new Nobel laureates identified the dispatcher molecules that direct that traffic

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-JCB, הדינמיקה המדעית שרותמן ושקמן יצרו נתנה לתחום מיקוד והתרגשות.
claims.quote: Particularly in the case of Rothman and Schekman, the scientific dynamic they helped to generate gave the field focus and excitement, from which came great things.

claims.text: לפי בריטניקה, רותמן זכה בפרס גרדנר הבינלאומי ב-1996 ובפרס לאסקר ב-2002, שניהם יחד עם שקמן.
claims.quote: the 1996 Gairdner Foundation International Award (with Schekman), the 2002 Albert Lasker Basic Medical Research Award (with Schekman)

claims.text: לפי אתר פרס קאבלי, רותמן קיבל את פרס קאבלי למדעי המוח ב-2010 ובהמשך את פרס נובל ב-2013.
claims.quote: After receiving the 2010 Kavli Prize in Neuroscience for discovering the molecular basis of neurotransmitter release, he received the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine

claims.text: רותמן נבחר לחבר זר ב-Royal Society של לונדון ב-2019.
claims.quote: was elected Foreign Member of the Royal Society of London (2019)

claims.text: רותמן עבר ב-1988 לפרינסטון, למחלקה לביולוגיה מולקולרית.
claims.quote: Rothman moved in 1988 to Princeton University in the Department of Molecular Biology

claims.text: לפי הביוגרפיה של נובל, ב-2004 הצטרף רותמן לקולג׳ לרופאים ולמנתחים של קולומביה.
claims.quote: In 2004, Rothman joined the Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons as a professor in the Department of Physiology and Cellular Biophysics

claims.text: לפי הודעת נובל, רותמן הוא פרופסור ויושב ראש המחלקה לביולוגיה של התא בייל.
claims.quote: where he is currently Professor and Chairman in the Department of Cell Biology

claims.text: לפי אתר פרס קאבלי, רותמן הוא פרופסור ויושב ראש המחלקה לכימיה בייל.
claims.quote: James E. Rothman is Professor and Chairman in the Department of Chemistry at Yale University.

claims.text: רותמן נשוי ויש לו בת ובן.
claims.quote: James Rothman is married with one daughter and one son.

claims.text: רותמן כתב שרעייתו ג׳ויס הירש הייתה מבקרת ותומכת בשנים הראשונות שבהן עבודתו לא התקבלה כפי שהיא מתקבלת היום.
claims.quote: has been my critic and supporter through the many early years when my work was not accepted as it is now

claims.text: רותמן צולם עם ילדיו באולם הקונצרטים בשטוקהולם מיד אחרי טקס פרס נובל ב-10 בדצמבר 2013.
claims.quote: on the stage in the Concert Hall in Stockholm, immediately after the conclusion of the Nobel Prize Ceremony, December 10, 2013

claims.text: רותמן נפגש עם הנשיא אובמה במפגש של זוכי נובל אמריקאים ובני זוגם ב-2013.
claims.quote: just after the meeting of the American Nobel Laureates and spouses with President Obama

claims.text: רותמן כתב שהשערה שפיתח עם גרהאם וורן בסטנפורד התבררה כנועזת אך בסופו של דבר שגויה.
claims.quote: on what turned out to be a bold but ultimately ill-conceived hypothesis that we had convinced ourselves was the key to the sorting problem

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-JCB, פרשנויות מסוימות של רותמן היו שנויות במחלוקת, אך לא הייתה מחלוקת על חשיבות הרכיבים שזוהו.
claims.quote: but there was absolutely no controversy regarding the importance of the various components he and his team identified

claims.text: לפי המאמר ב-JCB, העיקרון הבסיסי שמנגנון ההובלה אוניברסלי לא נחלש למרות המחלוקות לאורך השנים.
claims.quote: Through whatever controversies bubbled up over the years, this basic fact remained unchallenged.

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-JCB, בפרס יכלו להיכלל גם אחרים, למשל שלר וניוויק, אך רק שלושה מותרים והשלושה שנבחרו ראויים בהחלט.
claims.quote: It is certainly the case that others, for example Scheller and Novick mentioned here, might just as easily have been included in this award.

claims.text: לפי סקירה ב-PMC, יש הטוענים שחקר ההובלה התוך-תאית הוא תחום בשל, אך הכותב סבור שהוא רחוק מלדעוך.
claims.quote: my opinion is that the field of intracellular traffic research is far from waning or démodé

claims.text: לפי אתר בית הספר לרפואה של ייל, רותמן כיהן כיושב ראש המחלקה לביולוגיה של התא (2008–2023).
claims.quote: the former Chair of the Department of Cell Biology (2008-2023)

claims.text: אביו, מרטין רותמן, היה רופא ילדים, ורותמן תיאר אותו כרופא של עיירה קטנה בעל נטייה אינטלקטואלית.
claims.quote: My father Martin was an intellectually oriented small-town physician

claims.text: אביו, מרטין רותמן, היה רופא ילדים, ורותמן תיאר אותו כרופא של עיירה קטנה בעל נטייה אינטלקטואלית.
claims.quote: She ran the home and my Dad's pediatric practice and taught me how to organize and manage.

claims.text: פגמים בתהליך ההובלה מובילים למגוון מצבים, ובהם סוכרת ובוטוליזם.
claims.quote: Defects in this process lead to a wide variety of conditions, including diabetes and infectious diseases such as botulism.

claims.text: ב-2003, כשעזב את סלואן-קטרינג
claims.quote: Dr. Rothman spent more than a decade of his career at Memorial Sloan Kettering, from 1991 to 2003, where he did much of his seminal research.

claims.text: ב-2003, כשעזב את סלואן-קטרינג
claims.quote: Dr. Rothman also joins the faculty as a professor in the Department of Physiology and Cellular Biophysics.
